utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, good morning to you. Would you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam. Mr. Oric, can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen. Yes, I can follow the proceedings in my mother tongue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you. Yes, presentations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution. I'm here together with co-counsel, Ms. Patricia Sellers and Mr. Gramsci Di Fazio, as well as our case manager, Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink. And also good morning to my learned friends from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Wubben, and good morning to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, my learned friends from the OTP. My name is Vasvija Vidovic, and together with John Jones I appear for Mr. Naser Oric. With us is our legal assistant, Ms. Adisa Mehic, and our CaseMap manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic, and good morning to you and your team. Any preliminaries? Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, to clarify, with respect to P88 which we discussed yesterday, that was the form, I wish to state clearly that we challenge the authenticity of these documents from the outset. In connection with this, the OTP is in possession of the statement of a witness who was not called to testify here but whose name is listed on the form. Secondly, in their exhibit list the OTP stated that they would use 515 [as interpreted] and they wish to speak of this without the presence of the witness. P15 is the document containing the handwriting and the alleged signature of Dzenan Dzenanovic. This witness has given a statement and even the Dutch expert has stated that these signatures did not correspond to the signatures of Dzenan Dzenanovic. I wish to state this for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have anything to state on that, Mr. Wubben?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. There was also one document yesterday or the day before that you wanted to make -- no, yesterday there was one document that you said you wanted to contest the authenticity of and I stopped you, I said not in the presence of the witness, leave it for later. Perhaps you want to do that now?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can't remember the number or the exhibit number, to be honest with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: It was in handwritten form. I just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I know, but it was never really formalised because I stopped you straight away and I said not in the presence of the witness, leave it until later. And I would imagine it's the same document that Ms. Vidovic is talking about. If you want to register your opposition, your objection, to the admissibility of that statement, please do so now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to come back to that issue later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Any further preliminaries? I see none.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we can bring in the witness. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Dedic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again we are going to proceed with the direct, with the examination-in-chief, which should finish very soon. And then Madam Vidovic will be followed by Mr. Wubben with his cross-examination. Just to remind you of a few things: First, that you are testifying under oath or pursuant to your solemn declaration. Secondly, if there is a fault or any concern with regard to the reception of the interpretation, please come forward straight away, do let us know straight away, because we are not in a position to know whether you or someone else points that to us. Yesterday there was one instance when, had it not been for Madam Vidovic, we would not have known that you were not following. That's number two. Number three is if you really want to go back home after tomorrow, or by the end of tomorrow, or finish your testimony by then, try to keep your answers as brief as possible. I noticed that yesterday you were giving longer answers than on the previous -- than on the previous day and you were giving information that you were not actually being asked for. So please try to restrain yourself and restrict your answers to what is being asked from you. Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Dedic.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday we left off when discussing the issue of the existence of the military police and the security organ in Srebrenica during the years 1994 and 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to ask the usher to show the witness document D280.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document issued by the command of the 28th Division, security department, dated the 18th of April, 1995, and it is addressed to the security department of the 2nd Corps in Tuzla. It is an overview of the security situation, and I will quote to you a part of the document. This is in the middle of the first page, and it reads as follows: "The process of reorganisation has not yet been completed. The security section had not been brought up to manpower level. The military police company and other organs of the 28th Division have not been fully manned, which, if one takes into account that there is no military court or military prosecutor's office in these parts, makes work much more difficult. When one adds to this the fact that many of the officers are not professional and have been appointed to inappropriate posts, all this means that the functioning of the command and control system has been disabled." This document speaks of the process of the reorganisation of the Operations Group of Srebrenica into the 28th Division. Please, with respect to what was actually happening on the ground in Srebrenica and what you called your brigade, the reorganisation referred to here, that is from the Operations Group into the 28th Division, did it bring about any changes on the ground?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It only brought a change of name. Instead of the 8th Operations Group, it was called the 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But in essence, did the level of organisation remain the same?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely nothing changed in the organisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does this document reflect the actual situation on the ground, that the security section was not fully manned, the military police company or the other organs of the 28th Division were not fully manned?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, according to what you know and what it says here in this document, that most of the officers were not properly trained?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I fully agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said yesterday that the acronym RiK stands for command and control. Please, is it correct what it says here in this document, that the command and control system was unable to function under these conditions?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's completely correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: For example, the unit that you referred to as a brigade, did it have an organ or personnel trained to collect the information necessary for the prosecution of criminal offences and hand them over to the brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the list of military-able men that we were compiling - I'm referring to the 284th Brigade - there was one person -- there was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Not a single person.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- able to do this job properly. There was one man who was not properly trained.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us the name of that person and exactly what he was by profession?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was -- his name was Fadil Dedic and he was schooled in mining. This had nothing to do with the kind of work you're talking about. I'm sure that to this very day he doesn't know what a criminal investigation entails.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, in your testimony you describe the many crimes and murders that you heard had occurred against Muslims or that you saw or maybe you just heard about from others. Did you have any knowledge that investigations were carried out within the military structures or any organs in Srebrenica with respect to crimes against Muslims, for example?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never heard that there was any kind of investigation of crimes committed against Muslims in this period.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: While you were in Srebrenica, were you an eyewitness to large-scale massacres of the Muslim population there?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was an event in April 1994 - I don't remember the exact date - in front of the school where between 60 and 70 civilians were either killed or seriously wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, the authorities in Srebrenica, whether military or civilian, to the best of your knowledge - and I'm referring especially to the military authorities - did they conduct any kind of investigation about this incident or did they investigate where the shell came from, for example?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no investigation because there were no conditions to carry out an investigation. We didn't have trained personnel or any other conditions to conduct this type of investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, in what you called a brigade, and you were the chief of that brigade, did you receive any information about any crime against Serbs or their property?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never received any information of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: My colleague has drown my attention to a part of the transcript when we were talking about Fadil Dedic. Can you clarify what Fadil Dedic's position was supposed to have been in the so-called 284th Brigade. What was he supposed to be doing there?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was supposed to be doing security work. What exactly this is and what his job entailed, I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I just wanted to clarify this point.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Madam Vidovic. Before you -- however, I pass the witness on to Mr. Wubben for cross-examination, reading through the summary that you handed to us about this particular witness, there is one area, one paragraph, which describes him as the Chief of Staff of the 243rd Municipal Brigade. Is that a mistake or -- because it has not occurred. I mean, if you look at -- I'm sorry I'm bringing this up now, but I just wanted to make sure whether we ought to give it any importance or whether we ought to ignore it completely. In the summary, the Defence witness summary, you said, as the Chief of Staff of the 243rd Municipal Brigade, he will testify about the methodology, et cetera. Is that a mistake?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That's what I wanted to know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If it wasn't, I was going to either ask you to address it or then we would have addressed it ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, for drawing my attention to this. This brigade did not exist. Probably it must be a typing error, our error that is, an error made by us. What is correct is what the witness said today and it's quite clear in the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not a problem in the least, Madam. I -- it's just for a matter of clarification. Yes. So, Mr. Wubben, you can now start crossing the -- cross-examining the witness. Now, for your information, the Prosecution took exactly five hours and 40 minutes. That is -- the Defence, sorry, thank you. The Defence took exactly five hours and 40 minutes' time to examine in chief. So they were exactly well within the time limits. So you need to be within the time limit, too, which basically means you need to finish by tomorrow. Right. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. My name is Jan Wubben -- my name is Jan Wubben, as already mentioned by the Presiding Judge yesterday. I have questions for you this morning. I would like to invite you to be limited in your answers. I prefer a "yes" or "no" or an "I don't know." When I need a more extensive answer, I will indicate it to you by an open question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Adding -- adding to that. If, however, on any question after you are required to say -- answer yes or no, you think it's the case of explaining further, please address us straight away, the three Judges, and tell us so much and we will decide whether to give you permission to explain further or not, all right? Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Wubben, you can -- you may start.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Mr. Dedic, yesterday you explained to the Trial Chamber that you were a member of the Skugrici group. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That group, that unit, started from the beginning of war under the command of Mirsad Sulejmanovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: His nickname was Skejo?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And you also stated that you had no particular position in this group, except for the fact that you were a member.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: May I ask the usher now to show the witness a document, ERN 0837907 [sic] up to 018307910 [sic]. The English version is on Sanction, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is, I take it, a new document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Witness, I refer to this document. It is a request for joining the active military service of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and promotion to rank. Do you have the B/C/S version in front of you?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, my attention is being drawn, although I knew it already, that although you said it's on Sanction, it's not an Sanction.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I apologise. Please bear me a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not your fault, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is indeed a technical problem. We try to solve it by contacting the technicians, but in the meanwhile we can put it on the Sanction -- on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Usher, please, if you could assist with that. Thank you, Usher, and thank you, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Mr. Dedic, will you please take a look at the document, and let's first start not with the first page but the page 01837909. It is the third page -- it's the third page in English. Do you recognise the -- do you recognise your name down under that form?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is that -- has this been filled in by you?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Did you sign for this form?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the same page. In the right-hand corner you can see my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Let's move to the first page of this document. There it is, your name, your last name, Dedic, and father's name Ramiz, your first name, Ejub, and subsequently it has been filled in up to question or paragraph 39 on page 3. There, and I quote, it is stated: "Engagement on the preparation and organisation of armed conflicts before the war." Can you read it?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're talking about number 39, aren't we?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. And I quoted it. And my question is: Can you read it, what I quoted?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Did you fill in, and I quote: "Actively involved in collecting resources for purchasing of weapons and ammunition and leading activities not to hand over the weapons by any price"?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, can you repeat your question in relation to this. What are you asking me about what is written under number 39?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: My first question was: Did you fill in the -- that information that I just quoted?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What do you mean by "actively involved in collecting resources for purchasing of weapons and ammunition"?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In view of the fact that in my statement that I gave yesterday, we -- I mentioned that we bought part of our weaponry in order to be able to resist enemy attacks, I participated in that, in the collection of some resources. And therefore, we managed to buy some weapons in that period before the war itself broke out, that is to say in the situation when we had an imminent threat of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Does that mean that you yourself was involved in buying weapons and ammunition?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I personally was not involved in purchasing weapons. I said that I helped out in collecting money to buy it. Sabo Dedic, a relative of mine, bought a rifle from the Roma in Nova Kasaba, for instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. How many weapons were bought that way?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember only that one rifle, and I took part in buying that one rifle only. I don't know exactly, but I think about 100 pieces of ammunition for it, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So when it comes to the preparation and organisation of armed conflict before the war, you stated that you were actively involved in collecting resources for purchasing of weapon as being helping out in buying one weapon?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Active work in collecting resources has to be viewed from the position of the imminent danger. And I went around, talked to people, and said that it was necessary to buy as many weapons as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: But the outcome of that energy you put in, into actively being involved, that ended up in buying one weapon?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I personally, together with him, Mr. Sabo Dedic, went out and we bought a rifle, the one that I mentioned, and about a hundred or a couple of hundred pieces of ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So why did you then stated that there were weapons purchased and not one weapon?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mentioned the purchase of weaponry in the broader area, that is to say the enclave of Cerska. I mentioned yesterday that weapons were bought from a certain Serb called Gacic. So that was not the only rifle that was bought in the entire area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Were these weapons meant for the unit of Skugrici?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only this rifle that was bought in Nova Kasaba, yes. The other rifles were in the hands of the local groups, and those were the ones bought from Mr. Gacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yesterday you stated there were about -- and then I referred to the group of Mirsad Sulejmanovic, that they had around May a total of 30 weapons. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that that is correct, around 30 weapons in the group of Mirsad Sulejmanovic, Skejo, the beginning of the war, that is to say the beginning of spring and summer 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Let's move to issue 40, or paragraph 40. A question: The date of joining the RBiH armed forces. You joined the forces the 5th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The correct date of my joining the armed groups is the 6th of April, 1992. Now, how come it says the 5th? I don't know, I made a mistake perhaps, but it was the 6th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That one -- that's one day that might be -- that might be a mistake, but what is definitely clear that you joined the Crisis Staff of Cerska, the Vlasenica municipality. Can you clarify that?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Crisis Staff in Cerska was actually a group of people that often met and tried to explain how difficult the times were. And they were trying to propose certain solutions in order to avoid a war in the area. So it was not any kind of staff from the point of view of military organisation; this was a group of a few persons who met from time to time, debated, discussed the situation that awaited us in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So your testimony is that by the 6th of April, 1992, you joined the RBiH armed forces by participated in the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. One moment. Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do not recall having heard that he said the armed forces of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. He's talking about the Crisis Staff in Cerska.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I object to that remark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think there are two things that need to be clarified. Number one is that under number 40, at least in the English version, because I can't confirm by reading the Serbo-Croat one completely. What I have here is: "Date of joining the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina," and then in brackets, it says: "Name the body you applied to." To me it doesn't mean -- mention the body or the division or whatever in which you were actively engaged; it just indicates or requires the indication of the -- of the body the application was made to. That's how I understand it to be, at least reading the English version. If the Bosnian -- if the original version says anything different, please clear that straight away because we will need to know. That's number one. And secondly, there seems to be a misunderstanding between the two parties here. I did -- the question that has been put repeatedly is in relation to him accepting the correctness of the entry here, namely the 5th, now we are told it's the 6th, of April, 1992, as being the date which he joined the armed forces of RBH. So that -- if you think that is not clear according to you, we can go through this transcript, see whether it's clear or not. And if it's the case of proceeding further with further questions, we will of course have further questions. Or if you're not satisfied, you can deal with that during the re-examination. Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, lest there be any greater misunderstanding, the question in number 40 is: "Date of joining the RBiH armed forces," but the witness said he joined the Crisis Staff of Cerska, which is not a military organ. And Mr. Wubben proceeds as if the witness accepted that he joined the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Witness, am I right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I protest -- I object against this proceeding so far because Defence counsel, my learned friend, surely doesn't wish to guide the witness in any effect, I trust.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: The outcome will be that the witness is guided while his testimony is very clear and the answer was also very clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The thing is you may have misled him yourself, actually, Mr. Wubben, because if you look at line 15 on page 14. I'll give you time to track that. After that, the witness had corrected the date from the 5th of April to the 6th of April, 1992. Then you put the following question to him: "That one, that's one day that might be a mistake. But what is definitely clear is that you joined the Crisis Staff of Cerska, the Vlasenica municipality. Can you clarify that?" And then he answered: "Yes." So I take it that he did join the Crisis Staff of Vlasenica, of Cerska. And he continues: "The Crisis Staff in Cerska was actually a group of people that often met and tried to explain how difficult the times were and they were trying to propose certain solutions in order to avoid a war in the area. So it was not any kind of staff from the point of view of military organisation; this was a group of a few persons who met from time to time, debated, discussed the discussion that awaited us in that period." And then you proceeded with the question: "So your testimony is that by the 6th of April, 1992, you joined the RBiH armed forces by participating in the Crisis Staff." And then there was the -- I said -- I notice -- I recognised Ms. Vidovic standing up. But the witness in the meantime, before Ms. Vidovic spoke, said "Yes." So I think that the clarification that is in order, appropriate, now is the following: You are submitting to the witness, Mr. Wubben, that on the 6th of April of 1992, by joining the Cerska Crisis Staff was actually joining the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, as per self declaration contained in paragraph 40. The witness, however, has explained that the Crisis Staff he mentioned was not - and this is what he says on line 21 on page 14 - was not any kind of staff from the point of view of military organisations. So the explanation that we require is the following: If according to you, Mr. Dedic, the Crisis Staff of Cerska at the time you filed the application to join was not the kind of military staff from a point of view of military organisation, how can you explain that by filing an application with the Crisis Staff or by joining the Crisis Staff in Cerska you were actually joining the armed forces of the RBiH? Yes, Mr. Jones, if it helps to clarify. Otherwise, no comments until he answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No. No, Your Honour. It's simply -- I do think this point has to be made: In your summary just now Your Honour said that the witness had replied "Yes," in the meantime, to the question. I heard that he was saying something else as well. He had added some additional words which weren't interpreted. So in fairness, it wasn't simply "Yes," and we can check that, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's -- I think that's extremely important, Mr. Jones, because when that happens obviously we are not in a position to do anything. So I suggest, basing myself from experience, to go through it as follows: Mr. Wubben, you please repeat to the witness the same question that you put to him earlier on, which is the following: "So your testimony --" Mr. Dedic, this is the question that you are going to answer now: "So your testimony is, Mr. Dedic, that by the 6th of April, 1992, you joined the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina armed forces by participating in the Cerska Crisis Staff." Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I did take part in the work of the Crisis Staff from the 6th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And do you accept that by doing that you were -- you had automatically from that very same moment you started doing work -- working with the Cerska Crisis Staff, that you had for all intents and purposes joined the RBiH armed forces? Because this is what this document at least alleges that you indicated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. It is stated clearly here the date when I was made available, that is to say that on that date I did not become -- from that moment I was not engaged, as it says in the document, in the armed forces of the RBiH. I repeat, the Crisis Staff was not a military institution, a military organisation; it was a group of people that met from time to time in order to try to resolve the situation and in order to avoid the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Dedic. Mr. Wubben, I intervened a little bit to try and make it easier for everybody to understand, but I think we have arrived at a point now where we should not involve ourselves any further and I hand him back to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Let's move to question number 41. There the question is: "The date of engagement in the RBiH army and the name of the units, the duty and date of engagement." Is it correct that you filled in as a date the 15th of April, 1992, 3rd Company of the 1st Cerani - if I pronounce it well - Detachment?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you just want me to answer that part of the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes or no, as I invited you in the beginning of the cross.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I filled out this entry, number 41, the 15th of April, 1992, the 3rd Company of the 1st Cer Detachment. And then further on: Deputy commander of a company, chief of -- well, what is this? Probably Secretariat of People's Defence. I filled this entry out differently and the person who gave me the questionnaire threw it away. What I wrote was that I was engaged in the group of Mr. Sulejmanovic from the 15th of April, 1992, in Skugrici, and that sometimes when he was absent I stood in for him and that I listed military-able men in the area. However, the person who gave me the questionnaire to fill out threw that away and he guided me to write down what is written here. I told you yesterday that in the area of Cerska and in the area of Skugrici, there weren't any companies, there weren't any detachments. I did not have any duty in the group of Mr. Sulejmanovic or did I ever work in the secretariat that is mentioned here, except that I helped in keeping records of men who were in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Why did he throw it away?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me that something like that could not be there, because on the list we had to have names of units from a military point of view, not what I had written out for him the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So why did you -- and why did you abide by it?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he didn't want to accept the text that I had originally written.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And where did you originally written it?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I filled this out in Tuzla. I think it was at Dom Armije, the army hall in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: When you -- when you signed for this -- no. I withdraw that question. But you indeed signed for this form, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So in your testimony, it would be enough to sign for company deputy commander or for the 1st Cerani Detachment, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was never deputy commander of a platoon. I've never actually heard of the existence of platoon commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: But how come that person could advise you to full it in like this? How did he knew of the existence of such a company, if so?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday, while giving my explanations here, as far as I can remember I said that over there in Cerska, either at Tuzla or other places, individuals wrote down the names of armed groups the way they thought they should be called. So they mentioned the Territorial Defence, they mentioned detachments, they mentioned other units. So probably they had a reason to write it this way because somebody had already been calling those units that. I repeat once again: I cannot say that these Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. were units from a military point of view, that -- the way it's stated here. I'm not denying the fact that I was a member of armed groups, but not under the names mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And you don't deny that from the 15th of April, 1992, you indeed engaged in the RBiH army?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In that period I was engaged in these groups, and my engagement continued from then on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And you also confirm now in your clarification that you signed for a filling-in of the form that is partly incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Let's go into private session for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Please proceed, Mr. Wubben. I'm sorry to have interrupted you, but as you can imagine, this was -- my intervention was important.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will proceed by asking you -- it might be -- it might seem a repetition but it is good for clarification, that you can confirm to the Trial Chamber that you indeed engaged in the RBiH army from the 15th of April, 1992. Can you confirm?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So it means that, according to issue number 44, you completed in 1992 -- no --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will rephrase that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: In issue 44, the total pension of years of service are addressed and it was filled in as completed 12 years for the calculation of your pension. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This service in 44 covers the years of service I acquired working in a primary school before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you. And your pension is based on that?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on that and also my years of service in the professional military.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think -- sorry again to interrupt, but I think you have to look at the whole document. It seems it's divided into various -- there's up to January of 1979 where for a period of time he was employed in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 44 refers to a different period of time and to a different category of people, not people who are members of the former or were members of the former JNA, but people who were working in some other kind of activity not being the JNA. So what we have is here on the 26th of February, 1992, he is claiming to have acquired by then 12 years' service for pension purposes as an employ of the elementary school mentioned. Prior to that would apply the pension period acquired under the JNA, which is -- doesn't seem to be particular, but anyway. So don't mix 44 with what you have under 36 and 38.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: In issue 42, the question -- you confirmed that your actual position at the moment for signing is Chief of Staff of the 284th Light -- 284th Light East Bosnian Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And as you referred to yesterday, the officer's training, the compulsory officer's training, you achieved the rank of captain. Is that also correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. I was reserve captain. I acquired this rank in the JNA. At the beginning of 1992, before the war, I was a reserve captain.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That's what I -- that's what I meant. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I notice that page 24, line 17, there had been no interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but he did answer -- I heard him answer "Yes," so that goes into the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you finished with this document? Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, let's move to the detachment. The detachment I will refer to is -- bears ERN number 01837907 of the English, and so it should be 7910 as the last page of it, and the B/C/S version is 01837910. It is an opinion and proposal of the commander of the 8th Operation Group.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Who was at the time the commander of the 8th Operation Group, Witness?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time -- just a moment. Let me look at the date.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The 22nd is this 19 -- I don't know what date this refers to. Could you please repeat what period of time you're referring to when you ask me who the commander of the 8th Operations Group was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: The application is dated the 20th of February, 1994.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that time on paper, as I pointed out yesterday, the commander of the 8th Operations Group of Srebrenica was Mr. Oric.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And do you notice the name of Mr. Oric as commander of the 8th Operation Group on this form?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you know his signature?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't assert with full confidence that this was his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: This -- this form, this document, is signed by the -- by the commander of the 18th Operations Group, Srebrenica. And you refer to him, if you bear me a moment -- you said, and I quote it: "At that time he was commander on paper." What do you mean by that, he was a commander on paper?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said yesterday, and I wish to repeat it today, all the so-called brigades within the 8th Operations Group were actually a list of military-able men on the territory of Srebrenica proper.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: But does that mean that Mr. Oric was only signing papers because on paper he was a commander and didn't do anything else as being a commander?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No activities of the person who was a commander of my brigade on paper do I remember, let alone any activities by Mr. Oric.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: But are you aware of the fact that Mr. Naser Oric did do more than only signing papers? Did he play an active role at the time that you were in Srebrenica as a commander? What is your opinion about that?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll repeat my clear opinion to you: All the military activities in Srebrenica, apart from those of the international forces, were specifically banned. Srebrenica, according to my deep conviction, was an area without weapons, without armed men, without any kind of military activity by Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Does that mean that you are not aware that Mr. Naser Oric carried out any duties of a commander?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: What period are we talking about? He's obviously talking about demilitarisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perfect. I mean, I was actually looking at the Defence because I was expecting this. You need to be specific as to the date, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: More or less at the time that he has signed this document, according to what the Prosecution is alleging. Yes, Mr. Dedic, do you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So you -- could you give us an answer then, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question refers to the period of demilitarisation, 1994, in Srebrenica. In that period, I repeat again, there were no military activities by Muslims in this period.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So in your testimony, no military activities by the Muslim forces, and Naser Oric was a commander on paper only.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, let me go into this document signed by the commander of the 8th Operation Group, Naser Oric. And I quote: "Dedic (Ramiz) Ejub put himself at the disposal of the RBiH armed forces as a reserve captain from the 15th of April, 1992, and was engaged at the same time." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Is he asking if it's correct that it says that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would imagine that the -- what do you --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I don't --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, will you tell me where this text is? I'd like to take a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: It is the first --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Usher, please, could you help the witness. Make sure he's got in front of him the fourth page of the document ending with ERN 7910. Does he? All right. So that's the one. It's the first sentence, Mr. Dedic, where you have your name Dedic (Ramiz) Ejub "kao rezervni kapetan ..." That's the first sentence. And your question, Mr. Wubben, so that I don't put it myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you agree that that is correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is partly correct. Put himself at the disposal of, on the 15th of April, but I don't know that it was called the RBiH armed forces. It was at the disposal of the groups active in the areas of Skugrici and Cerska. We had no communication with any other forces in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. As for the date, that's correct, but at the disposal of the groups being formed in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: You were, in the opinion of this document, engaged in purchasing and handling of armaments and ammunition. You were organising people in the region of Skugrici, Vlasenica, and you distinguish yourself as an organiser of village guard. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said earlier that I participated in purchasing one rifle bought by a relative of mine - I helped him - and ammunition. I never dealt in trading in weapons. As for participating in -- engaging people, yes, but organising people in Vlasenica, no. But only insofar as Skugrici, a part of Vlasenica municipality. Distinguished himself as an organiser of village guards. The village guards were the first groups who, especially by night, patrolled around the villages and monitored the situation. So this part of the text is correct, but purchasing and handling of armament and ammunition, no, I never dealt with that. The re-sale of weapons, that is. But I was never active in Vlasenica. Vlasenica was cut off. I couldn't go there. This is correct only insofar as Skugrici is part of Vlasenica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now -- and I go back, that you made some clarification and nuances in this text. But anyhow, what states in the document that you were engaged in the RBiH armed forces from the 15th of April, 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just let him answer. I know what you're coming up with.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The date of engagement in armed forces, the 15th of April, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The question was whether he confirms that the document states that he was engaged in the RBiH armed forces from the 15th of April. Otherwise, he has explained his position on this. Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, his reply was misinterpreted. He keeps saying that this was engagement in armed groups, whereas here it's -- the interpretation is "armed forces."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Vidovic, that's why I said what the question was and what the answer was. The question was not what he got engaged in, but what -- he was asked whether it's correct that the statement by -- allegedly by Mr. Oric states that he was engaged on the 15th of April in the armed forces of Republic -- it's not whether he was engaged, whether the statement states so much. And of course he has answered yes, and that's a correct answer, because that's what the statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The reason I interrupt, Your Honour, was because earlier, and it didn't appear in the transcript, but Mr. Wubben said anyhow what states in the document correct. That hasn't come out and in the end, probably just as well, but it's suggested that there is a double question, does the document correctly state --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I don't have it on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, that's why I stood up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I knew what you were coming up with, I could anticipate, of course. But I stopped you because what I have in the transcript is what counts.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Also in terms of not misleading the witness, let's not overlook the fact that this is a request for joining the active military service of the army of ABiH. I'm sure it's a matter which Your Honours would have drawn attention to

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I object, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's the title of the document, the title of the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones is ultimately correct. Basically, this is a new phase in the life of the military career, if you can call it so, of Mr. Dedic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And because of a new phase in his life, in the career, I assume that Mr. Dedic filled in the form correctly and to the actual state and his history --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But this is now finished. Next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you want to challenge the honesty of the witness in as far as filling this document is concerned, you have every right to do so and you will be given all the opportunity to do so, with the caveats that I mentioned earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's something for a later phase, but what I noticed is that there is a misinterpretation of my -- of at least what I meant with the last question. So I will repeat it again but I will rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is -- regarding your comment on the document signed by the commander of the 8th Operation Group, the opinion and proposal of the commander, it is stated there that you put yourself at the disposal of the RBiH armed forces from the 15th of April, 1992. Is that true -- is that true, as the document says, that you were engaged in the RBiH army from the 15th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me repeat once again that the date is correct, but I can never agree that these were the RBiH armed forces. I was exclusively engaged in this period in the local groups gathered around the local leaders. The name people applied to this later on, that's something different. I can't change people's opinion about the names of those groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you. I will move to the next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But we need to give it a number.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. Please assign an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We need to give this document a number, an exhibit number. Can you give me the next number, please. P --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P581, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So this document, which consists of four pages in B/C/S and four pages in the corresponding translation into English, ERN 01837907 through 01837910, both numbers included, is being tendered and received and marked as Prosecution Exhibit P581. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: May I ask the usher to show the witness document ERN DA17-7864. This is a type proposal for the promotion of the rank of major. And I quote that it's referring to the last name, father's name, and first name, to Dedic (Ramiz) Ejub.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is it correct, if you notice, the personal background, that it refers to you, this document?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dedic (Ramiz) Ejub, yes. Born on the 1st of March, 1957, yes. Place and municipality of birth: Skugrici, Vlasenica, yes. Place of residence, street and number. This refers to 1995, so Srebrenica, yes. Nationality, Bosnian Muslim, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you. And now question number 10: Duties performed so far in the RBiH: Deputy commander, deputy -- company commander, commander, company chief of the Defence Secretary in the surrounding detachment. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These, in my view, are practically the same questions. I wish to say that I was in the group, and occasionally, when Mr. Sulejmanovic was absent, he would ask me to stand in for him. But the position of deputy company commander never existed as such because it was not a proper company in the military sense. I wish to emphasise this. The company commander, if I see well, and as far as I know as a soldier, the expression used in B/C/S for company commander is "komandir," not "komandant." And as for Chief of Staff, I wish to say that in Cerska there were very few literal -- people who were literate. Most of the literate people had left, so it was, unfortunately, up to me to write things down. So somebody wrote that this was the Secretariat of Defence, but there was actually never any kind of Defence Secretariat in Cerska, either before the war or during the war. So this information under 10 is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Under 11, is it true, you were the brigade Chief of Staff 1995?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In January.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. As we said, several times on paper, I was Chief of Staff. I myself participated in drawing up this document. I was Chief of Staff of the 274th East Bosnia Light Brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction; 284th.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is it also correct that under 15 and as later on in the document down under, you particularly distinguish yourself in the advancement of the organisation and defence power of the republic's armed forces?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, can I just read this briefly, what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Proposed for promotion because he was in the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina from the beginning of the war where he conscientiously performed all his duties. He particularly distinguished himself in the advancement of the organisation and defence power of the republic's armed forces. In the military unit he was employed on improving interpersonal relations and increasing of combat morale as an exemplary -" what does it say here - this is not the Bosnian language, exemplary. "He enjoys selfless loyalty --" the selfless trust, that is, "of soldiers and officers alike." This is the first time that I have seen I was so good. Had I been such a good soldier, I would probably have been the commander of a large unit. I would have been a brigadier and the commander of a division perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: May I ask you -- the question was in fact: Did you advance -- did you contribute to the advancement of the organisation and the defence power of the republic's armed forces? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I participated in the armed groups, and I can't really say how much I was able to help.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And were you indeed promoted to the rank of major?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was promoted to the rank of major --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- in 19 -- it was later on, after this period, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I have an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This document, which consists of two pages in B/C/S and another two pages in English with ERN DA17-7864, is being tendered by the Prosecution, received, and marked as Prosecution Exhibit P582.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's time for a time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll have a 30-minute break, starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I understand you want to raise a matter, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I wish to raise the question of the constant violation of Rules 68 and 66(B) as far as the Office of the Prosecutor is concerned. I will be talking about document P81. This document was not -- the document number is P551. This document had not been disclosed to us until last night. We could not --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 581, Your Honour. P581.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It sounded strange, because in the transcript we had 551 and I couldn't fit that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, 581 and 5812. Yes. 581 for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 581, Your Honour. First of all, the documents that are on EDS and were handwritten, several times when talking to the OTP I told them that the computer cannot recognise them and -- anyway, we received it only last night. I'm quite convinced that this is a document that belongs to the category of the previous statement of the witness, and we asked for these documents to be submitted to us in accordance with Rule 66(B). Obviously, they do fall under 66(B) and we are entitled to have them and we have the right to prepare the Defence of our client as best possible. Several times during the course of this trial, Mr. Wubben, the Prosecutor, talked about surprise tactics. That is what they've been trying to do all the time. Your Honours, once again I request that all these documents that have to do with previous witness statements and everything that would belong to that category, and documents that have to do with our witnesses and that we need in order to prepare our Defence, that they be submitted to us immediately and in a timely fashion. Even before we received this document, we sent them a very definite letter along those lines. But, quite simply, they are not honouring that. They do disclose or do not disclose. You caution them, and this has been going on forever, and we are not in a position to prepare our Defence as we could if we had all the documents made available to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What's your position on this, Mr. Wubben? Before you do so, you also mentioned when you started, Ms. Vidovic - just for the record, that's all in line 20 of the previous page, page 35 - you also mentioned Rule 68.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Rule 68 does not pertain to this document; however, very soon we will be addressing the Trial Chamber again with a motion that will have to do with Rule 68. We are expecting another response from the Prosecutor in that sense. But specifically now I was talking about Rule 66(B).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Wubben, the allegation is that, although you are bound by Rule 66(B) to "... permit the defence to inspect any books, documents," et cetera, on request, "which are material to the preparation of the defence, or are intended for use by the Prosecution as evidence at trial or were obtained from or belonged to the accused," that by not making this document, 581, available to the Defence in good time, instead of yesterday, you've violated the provision that I have just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, I will give an answer to that, but first I object to the use of the word "surprise attacks" or something like that that we would have mentioned or used earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's stick --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And as far as I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- to this --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I would rather keep it professionally. And indeed to answer your question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you want to answer now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, now. We disclosed -- we disclosed this document indeed yesterday. We add to it that in an earlier phase we already disclosed it, and we had receipts of numbers of those disclosing. Those were referring to receipts 17 and 51 respectively. So we disclosed it, and already pointed out in an earlier phase we disclosed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I didn't get this. 17 and 51, what's this? P -- let's talk about P581. You're saying that you had disclosed this to the Prosecution -- to the Defence earlier on?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, in an earlier stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you be more precise?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: We disclosed it yesterday because they asked for it, so it was redisclosed. And in the letter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: -- in which we updated them that we already redisclosed -- already disclosed it in the past, we add to it, for their courtesy, again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How had you disclosed it in the past?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In paper format; in hard copy, in other words?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please bear me a moment. It was done via CD, and we have a receipt number, and that number is 17, and I was referring to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And if I understood you well, you were complaining, Ms. Vidovic, that in the electronic database the script, as I understood it, if not always sometimes the print, does not show up in a legible manner. Does this apply also to the CD that was, according to the Prosecution, handed to you as per receipt number 17 or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we usually have very precise information. I think the answer is no, but we'll check the CD. However, what I said before, when a handwritten document is submitted electronically, then it is not possible to find it according to the criterion, say, Ejub Dedic, because the computer absolutely does not recognise handwritten documents. Believe me, Your Honour, this is what I've been telling them time and again. And quite simply, they've been turning a deaf ear to this. And in this way they've hindered the preparation of the Defence. It is only fair for us to be able to prepare our Defence in the best possible way. So if we ask for all previously given statements, this belongs to that category, and they were duty-bound to give it to us. If we had received it in electronic form, we were not in a position to recognise it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Wubben, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: If I may help out and support the Defence on my recent information, it was -- the receipt 17 was done on the 12th of November, 2003, referring to a CD, including various ERN numbers, and within the range of that particular document. So 12th of November, 2003 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, because I don't want to have this blown beyond proportions until it can be finalised. It's true that -- what Ms. Vidovic points out, that when you post this in the electronic database, what the system can search is what is printed and readable according to the soft ware and readable for the software. When it comes to script, written, it's practically almost 100 per cent impossible to conduct any search that would lead you to the document. However, in this particular case, and this is why I'm saying I don't want to blow it up beyond proportions at the present moment, the fourth page is not handwritten, the fourth page is printed. And it shows the name of the witness. So presumably, although I am saying this always subject to correction because, of course, I don't know what has happened in this case, by an ordinary search through the electronic database, one should at least locate this page. But it doesn't necessarily -- at least to my knowledge, it doesn't necessarily tie it up to the previous three documents because what you would find is just the fourth page and not also the previous three pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, that might be true when it comes to EDS as a technical approach, but definitely in this way --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's going to change --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: -- we provided them with a CD. So a CD in which easily can be done --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Vidovic is not categorically denying that you did. She said that she will be locating the CD and checking. And then if necessary, we will come back to this matter later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I hope anyhow that she will do it outside the court, because so far our aim was between the parties to solve any questions outside the court in order to support a smooth operation in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And I'm still pursuing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you both. Let's bring the witness in and try to move, because we are losing time, precious time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let me just put the witness's mind at rest that the reason why we are starting again somewhat later than I said has got nothing to do with you, Mr. Dedic. We just had a procedural problem that we needed to address. So sorry about that. Mr. Wubben can now proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Mr. Dedic, this morning, first session you were shown a document P581. I have a question in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: May I ask the usher to put the third page of the Serbian version on the ELMO, please. Can the usher please move to the bottom of the document, show -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Right under, Mr. Dedic, in the first session this morning your testimony was that you signed for this form, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is my signature at the end of the form.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And please leave that on the ELMO, Usher, and I would like to ask you to show the witness P88. Now will you, Madam Usher, please move to the -- show the witness the fourth page, the page with the names. And place it in such a manner next to the P581 that the name of Ejub Dedic is next to each other and shown in the centre of the ELMO. Can you please lower -- thank you. And to the right more. Yes. Thank you. Please leave it there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that this form had not been signed by you. Is that correct? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not sign this form. On the document up here, that is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dedic, I know you're not a handwriting expert, but doesn't it appear to be the same slanting backwards sloping writing when it comes to your name?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can't you put a much simpler question, Mr. Wubben? "Don't you see a similarity between the two?" Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Don't you see a similarity between the two names as written down there, your name?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're asking me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, I think he is asking you, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Can you -- indeed you should look at the ELMO and not on the screen. Did you take a look at the screen -- well, and will you now please take a look at the ELMO. On the ELMO there are two documents. Please, Witness -- I can't see the witness. Please, Mr. Dedic, can you take a look at me? Yes. Will you please take a look at the two documents in front of you on the ELMO and answer my question: Is there a similarity between the two names as written down there, your name?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Similarity between my name on the document where it says "date and place of filling out form, Ejub," and then --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Mr. Dedic. I'm sorry. On both documents your name are written. One document is document P581. You signed for it, and yesterday your testimony on the other document, P88, was: I did not sign that form. Now, my question is: You see -- you notice your name. Is there in this handwritten form a similarity between those two names as it is written down?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That's all, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The interpretation is still going. Your Honour, it's a big --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Choose who goes first.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's a major problem. I've noticed it time and again. I can hear the interpretation, maybe because my colleague is still going, and the witness says yes to the first part of the question and then that's taken as an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So what did you say yes to? Mr. Dedic, when you said "yes" a moment ago, what were you confirming?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That on both documents you can see my name and surname.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but the question wasn't whether you can see your name and surname on both documents. Whether your -- the way your name and surname appears in both these documents is similar or not, whether the handwriting is similar or not, basically. This is what you're being asked to answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a small similarity between the handwriting of the last name and there is no similarity in the handwriting of the first names on these two documents. I don't know whether I've been clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Your Honour. He gave a full answer and it simply did not enter the transcript. This is the answer that he gave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What he has just said now?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So you're telling us that he had said it before but it did not show up in the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know what to say. I know that there is a protocol how you're supposed to deal with problems with transcripts, and my attention has been drawn to that. But at the same time certain matters that arise during the sitting have to be addressed during the sitting. Yes, do you want to pursue this matter any further, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Usher. I would like to move to the following document: ERN DA17-0504. Will you please show that to the witness, Madam Usher. It's a new exhibit, Your Honour. For your information, it has been translated partly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Mr. Dedic, is this a document from the 28th Division command of the date of the 30th of March, 1995, and it is dealing with proposals of the Golden Lily badge war commendation. Is it true that you received Golden Lily badge war commendation?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never received the Golden Lily order.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Had you been recommended for such an order?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know no one had ever proposed me for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Let me move to the page -- let me move to the page where your name is stated. That's further on in the document, under number 1: Dedic (Ramiz) Ejub.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. What was the page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which DA17 number?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. I'll take a look at it, Your Honour. It's page DA17-0521.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So it's the page before the last page, basically, we are talking about. The last page or the page before at the very end.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, the page before the last. Okay. The -- about ten, 15 lines from the top. Have you find it -- found it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have. This is number 1 on the page before the last, where my name is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will now ask you questions related to that paragraph. It's stated: "He -" that's apparently you - "he joined the RBiH armed forces on the 15th of April, 1992, as a member of the 1st Cerani Detachment on the duty of deputy commander of the 3rd Company." And it follows as, I quote: "He then became the commander of the 8th Company and was performing this duty up until November 1992." Is that true, that you were also subsequently the commander of the 8th Company?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By your leave, I wish to mention here again that this is the first time I have heard of the 8th Company. I have never before heard of such a formation. Let me repeat once again, I do apologise --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. My question to you was very simple. Is it true or is it not true or you don't know whether or not you subsequently became the commander of the 8th Company and were performing your duty up until November 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just answer yes or no. It's true or it's not correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is it true --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I really feel that in such situations it's necessary for the witness to explain why not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That's why I didn't stop him myself actually. He was giving an answer. But anyway, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Mr. Dedic, is it true or not that after that you were appointed the chief of Secretariat of Defence of Vlasenica municipality?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He has explained this already, that to his knowledge there was no such Secretariat of Defence of Vlasenica municipality and he was not in Vlasenica in any case.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And is it true, Mr. Dedic, that you particularly distinguished yourself in the sabotage action of the Chetnik stronghold above the village of Vandjici in July of 1992?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Had there ever been such a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's -- one moment. What's not correct, that you particularly distinguished yourself in that sabotage action or that you actually did not take part at all in that sabotage action? What are you trying to tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was not there at all. I did not participate in that action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
