utterances.text: Is it true that you also participated with a number of other soldiers in a sabotage action on Metaljka on the 12th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct. On that occasion, together with a small group, I participated in the destruction of an enemy tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Were you a deputy commander of that group by then?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Did you also participated in the action on Ilino Brdo on the 8th of February, 1993?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. On the 8th of February, 1993, there were the fiercest attacks on the area where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is it true that you refused earlier the commendation of the Golden Lily out of modesty?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, I wish to repeat again: I was never proposed for the Golden Lily war commendation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, can this be assigned an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wubben. This document, which in the B/C/S version starts from DA17-0504 until DA17-0522, part of which has been translated into English, a copy consisting of two pages, is being tendered and received and marked as Prosecution Exhibit P583.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Usher, will you please provide -- show to the witness ERN 02123453.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: This document, Mr. Dedic, is dated the 9th of August, 1992. It's signed by Mr. Hodzic, page 3, as commander of the Vlasenica armed forces, and it is an order on appointing war deployment. I refer you to chapter B, capital "B/ On war duties in the 1st Cerani Detachment, I appoint and promote..." Do you read that?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Under paragraph 2: "Assistant commander for morale, education, Dedic, Ejub, son of Ramiz." Is that referring to you. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This does refer to me as far as my first and last name are concerned, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Did you finish the higher school of economics and SRO?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I completed the pedagogical school, not the economic -- not the school of economics.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And is it true that you were on war duty in the municipal Territorial Defence staff from the 15th of April, 1992, as stated?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, if you will allow me, I wish to comment on this very briefly, by your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to note -- I wish to note now that there was never any military staff there, nor did I ever work, as it says here, on the job -- or rather, I never performed any duty in the municipal Territorial Defence Staff from the 15th of April, 1992. As I mentioned, as of this date, I was part of a group, the leader of which was Mirsad Sulejmanovic, also known as Skejo, so my activities cannot be linked to any kind of staff. So the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: When I see the name of Mr. Hodzic, you are familiar with that name, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with the name of Hodzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: He was the commander of Vlasenica armed forces, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was able to write down that he was the commander of the Vlasenica armed forces. I couldn't prohibit him from doing that. But he was a group of a leader -- he was the leader of a group that arrived with him when it was expelled from Vlasenica and arrived in Cerska. He persistently attempted to unify all those groups, to bring them together, but in my view, he never succeeded in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Mr. Dedic, in Vlasenica, prior to his arrival in Cerska, he was commander?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Hodzic was the commander of the Territorial Defence staff in Vlasenica until the beginning of the war; that is, in peacetime.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And Vlasenica being the capital of the municipality, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So he was the commander of the armed forces, the TO, in Vlasenica, the capital of Vlasenica municipality, and he came with a lot of his men towards Cerska?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did arrive in Cerska in late May or early June with quite a few men, but with very few armed men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a distortion of what the witness is saying. The Prosecutor asked him whether he was the commander of the Territorial Defence staff before the war and the witness replied, yes, he was before the war. And then the Prosecutor goes on to ask: So he was the commander of the armed forces. These two questions have nothing to do with each other and they are confusing and misleading the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think they are that misleading or confusing. I think what the witness has said is very clear; that to him, Mr. Hodzic was commander of the Territorial Defence of Vlasenica before the war. After that, he came to Cerska and he pretended to continue to be so. This is how I have understood his testimony throughout. I mean, if --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If Mr. Wubben is not understanding it the way I am understanding, he's free, of course, to proceed with questions. But I don't think he's misleading the witness or -- I don't think so. Or at least, I haven't thought that in question --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I see from observing the -- both Judge Eser and Judge Brydensholt with me. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So Mr. Hodzic, and his first name is Ferid, isn't it, Ferid Hodzic?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Ferid Hodzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: He arrived in Cerska after the fall of Vlasenica, around the spring of 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He just said around about the end of May or June of 1992. That's what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I'm now referring to the fall of Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: When was the fall of Vlasenica, Mr. Dedic?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vlasenica fell in mid-April 1992, but these groups, that is a certain number of armed men, together with Mr. Ferid Hodzic, hid with a large group of refugees in the woods, hoping to be able to return to the town. When they realised they could no longer return to Vlasenica, after that they arrived in Cerska. That's why they arrived somewhat later than the fall of Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And Mr. Hodzic also brought weaponry and ammunition with him?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall seeing a small number of armed men who arrived with him. But Mr. Hodzic did not have any personal weapons on his arrival in Cerska.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And your testimony yesterday was that he tried to unite local groups that were active in Cerska, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Throughout this time, he kept trying to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: He tried, according to this letter, the heading -- he tried to improve the organisation formation structure and leadership and command system of the Vlasenica municipality armed forces, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I wish to repeat once again quite clearly, he was only trying to do this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So uniting them, those forces, under unitary or under one command, what it is?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The unifying of all the groups in the areas of Skugrici and Cerska under one command was never carried out. From the beginning of the war until the fall of these areas, they acted locally. They were active in the areas where they had been before the war. A joint command was never formed. They were never located in a single place. They never received and carried out orders --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I apologise to interrupt you, Mr. Dedic; that was not my question. My question was very simple: Did he try to unite these forces under one command or not? A simple "yes" or "no" or "I don't know" will do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, he did try.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the reason of such a uniting of groups --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Such an attempt. Let's be clear. In cross-examination one can put propositions but not ignore what the witness said --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Sorry, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Jones. Have you understood the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will repeat it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Can you tell me what is the background, what is the reason of such, of the policy of trying to unite the groups?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fundamental reason for the attempt to unify the local groups, in Mr. Hodzic's view, was that this would facilitate the defence of the Skugrici and Cerska areas where he was active along with the local groups.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What do you mean, Witness, by "facilitating the defence"?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the fact that Mr. Hodzic had some experience since he had worked in the Vlasenica Municipal Staff before the war, he probably had a vision according to which the unifying of all these groups would be a better solution and would lead to better results. That was his vision, that was his plan. But how he meant to carry it out, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: May I ask the usher to show the witness P123.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the meantime, let's give this document a number. The last document, this last document, which consists of two pages in B/C/S and three pages containing corresponding translation thereof into English, with ERN 02123453 to 4 is being tendered, received, and marked as Prosecution Exhibit P584.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Witness, do you have in front of you a report of the established staffs by Tuzla district, dated the 29th of August, 1992?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please bear me a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Will you please move to B/C/S page -- no. First -- that's not page 1. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. For me it's the page with ERN 01827482, starting with: "Pursuant to your order ..." Do you read that, Witness, Mr. Dedic?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't see it. I have document 01827482 [Realtime translation read in error "01826482"], but at the moment I can't see what you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will read the rest at issue --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is ERN 01827482.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, Usher -- yeah, yeah -- 82 -- he said, at least according to the transcript, 01826 and you are saying 827.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, yeah. But the difference between what you said and what he said is that one said 6 and the other one said 7. So I want to make sure that we're talking about the same. What does he have, 7 or 6?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Should be the first B/C/S page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 7. So you do have, according to the usher, the correct document, Mr. Dedic. Please again refer him now to this specific part of that page that he needs to look at.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Mr. Dedic, can you read, and I quote: "Pursuant to your order, strictly confidential number --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The beginning of the document, basically, the -- after the headings. Did you find it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Yes, yes, yes, I've been following, as the gentleman was reading. I found that part now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And I quote: "Please find enclosed the report on established staffs and unit of the armed forces of the Tuzla district." Can you read that?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the page bearing the number 01827485, at the end it says: "Municipal defence staff of Vlasenica." Is this it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will reiterate my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: On the first page of the report there is this paragraph you prior could read, starting with the words: "Pursuant to your order ..." Now, on the second line there's a reference to the report on established staffs and units of the armed forces of the Tuzla district. Can you read it, Mr. Dedic?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you. This -- on the last page of this report you find the name Commander Zeljko Knez. Can you read it?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was the page before last in my copy, Commander Zeljko Knez.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Dedic, that Zeljko Knez was at that time in August 1992 the commander of the Tuzla District Defence staff?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Zeljko Knez was the commander, but I'm not sure of the time period.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is it true that according to this report and the address addressed to, the Tuzla district reported to the staff of the Supreme Command of the armed forces in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the heading of the document it can be seen that the report was drawn up by the Tuzla District Defence staff. It's about the staffs established. I don't know to whom it was forwarded. It probably was forwarded to someone, since it was compiled, but by your leave, as there are quite a few municipal staffs here, he mentions the municipal defence staff of Vlasenica on page 01 --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Mr. Dedic, please. I apologise to interrupt, but the question really only focussed on your confirmation or not or you don't know to what address this report was addressed to. So please answer with yes or no: Had it been addressed to Sarajevo, the staff of the supreme command? Yes or no or you don't know.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know to whom this report was sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you read that the report is addressed to the staff of the Supreme Command of the armed forces in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. So it's clear that the confusion results from the ambiguity between, A, asking the witness to confirm what is stated in the document, which is largely unnecessary because we can all read for ourselves what the document says, and asking this witness to confirm that in fact this report was addressed or sent to Sarajevo. The witness has asked -- answered the second question, clearly he doesn't know whether or not it was received. If he's being asked merely to confirm that the document says what it says, then I don't see the point, because we can all read that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, when it comes to asking questions -- putting questions to a witness and when a lawyer is using a document, we first go through the background or the heading or whatsoever of the document and you try to ensure that the witness is reading what the document is about. And of course everybody could -- can read it. But the confirmation for the transcript is very important that the witness has read it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you, Mr. Wubben. But sometimes it gets confusing because witnesses themselves realise -- sometimes wonder why they are being asked to confirm what a document states when it should be clear to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, particularly because here the question was: "Had it been addressed to Sarajevo the staff of the Supreme Command, yes or no or you don't know?" Well, how can the witness not know what's in front of him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's a matter of -- the problem is English more than anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That suggests that the witness is being asked to give an answer based on his own knowledge not on just what the document says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's cut this short. What do you want to know from the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: On the second page, Witness, do you read the reference to Bratunac municipal staff?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Dedic, do you see it or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes, yes. On page 2: Municipal staff, Bratunac. Yes, yes, that is what is written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is it true that at the time of the report there was indeed a staff in the Bratunac municipal staff?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And is it true that there was a 1st TO detachment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In Bratunac, obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Still in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is a fact that I am unaware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And a second TO detachment?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I'm unaware of the existence of the second territorial detachment in the municipal staff in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Let us move to the page further on, dealing with the Vlasenica municipality defence staff. That's ERN 01827482. Do you read that, Mr. Dedic?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that's not the number I have here. But that is what it says: "Municipal staff of Vlasenica." 01827485 is the number I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: It's -- in the report, it's confirming as by August 1992 there was a staff. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is it true that there was a reconnaissance platoon?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And a protection headquarters company?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never heard of this company. As far as I know, I've never heard of any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And a Vlasenica TO detachment. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. TO Vlasenica detachment, no. Never existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And the Cerska TO detachment. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Cerska TO detachment never existed either.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: The Djile TO detachment, if I pronounce it correctly?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. It did not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: A 1st and 2nd Kladanj TO Company?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm allowing this because the same question was asked yesterday and he answered to each and every one of them, but I'm not quite sure whether the question he was asked yesterday was with reference to the 9th of August or not. So this is why I'm allowing you to finish this series of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because he went through this yesterday and he denied the existence of -- or the knowledge of the existence of any of these.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your answer is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was the same document or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Mr. Dedic, your answer is under 8, 9, and 10, these companies and detachment doesn't exist at the time?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My answer is that they did not exist. Let me just repeat this, Your Honour, by your leave. I really don't know whether there were any companies in Kladanj. Yesterday I mentioned that Kladanj is about 60 to 70 kilometres away from Cerska. And what particularly confuses me here is number 10, or rather, no, sorry, number 9. It says Pobudje TO Company. Again, I repeat that Pobudje was within the municipality of Bratunac before the war, and even today it is in the municipality of Bratunac. And this really has nothing to do with the municipality of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of Vlasenica. Yes, let's move, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: It correct that the municipality fell under the Tuzla district at the time?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is a question for me, I did not quite understand what the gentleman wished to ask me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Whether Vlasenica municipality formed part of the Tuzla district at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The municipality of Vlasenica at that time, that is to say before the war, was within the Tuzla district, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you. That's for this document. Mr. Dedic, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yesterday you stated that the Defence in Cerska had been organised locally.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The defence in Cerska had been organised at local level.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And there were smaller and bigger armed group that rallied around their leaders. True?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What do you mean by those armed units? How many were those when it comes to the area of Cerska?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness keeps talking about armed groups and Prosecutor Wubben keeps talking about armed units.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That doesn't really make --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will use the same words --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead. The important thing is that we are not confused in our mind, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: To be accurate, Your Honour, on page 6 of the transcript of yesterday, on top, line 3, the answer is, and I quote: "Yes, there were smaller or bigger armed units that rallied around their leaders."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you blow it up and it could become a problem of interpretation. Let's move, please. Be practical --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What do you mean by that, "rallied around their leader," and can you tell me the number of villages that had been organised like that?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can give you some. I'm not going to give you all, I'm quite sure, because I was not a person who was involved in these matters. But I know one thing for sure: That in Skugrici there was a group whose leader was Mirsad Sulejmanovic, Skejo. In Cerska, there was a bigger group that rallied around its leader, Semso Salihovic. Then a smaller group which rallied around Saban Muminovic. A group that came with Mr. Hodzic from Vlasenica rallied around him, and a group that had rallied around Mr. Besir Aljukic. And -- and a smaller group that was rallied around Fikret Mustafic and was active in the area of the villages that I mentioned yesterday, Tumace and Macesi. Perhaps there were some other smaller groups that I cannot recall at this moment, but at any rate these are the ones that I remember well now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: When you refer to those groups in the area of Cerska, the total number of those groups - and I don't mean strength or whatever - groups rallied around the leader, the total number, was that around 15 or 20, can you give an estimation to your best knowledge?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not give any estimate. These are the groups that I mentioned, and I am sorry -- I've just remembered the group of Mr. Mekanic that came in the summer of 1992. Yes. So at this moment I could not give Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the exact number of all these groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: But I don't ask you for an exact number. Let me just rephrase and ask you simply: Was it more than 20?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were certainly less than 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: More than 10?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now perhaps I could start all over again and write this down on paper so that I would not engage in guesswork, how many there were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I want to make sure that he is understanding or -- because I'm getting a little bit confused here. The question is a very simple one. These leaders that you have just mentioned coming from different places, each one of them, on an average, how many -- how many members of the group would rally around them? Say if -- on an average because I would imagine that they various varied from one to the other, but on average when we're talking about these six, seven, eight leaders that you mentioned having people rally around them, how many people would rally around each one of these seven, eight, nine, ten leaders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can tell you that according to my knowledge from later on, in the entire area there was about 2.000 military-able men, and before the fall of Cerska there were between 4 to 500 pieces of weaponry in their hands. That is the information that I can present to you at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have I made your life easier like that, Mr. Wubben?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: In addition, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please don't try to make mine more difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: How many villages were organised like that?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please clarify this question for me. Are you referring to the number of villages where these groups were active?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. Muslim villages in the Cerska area.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Almost in most villages, especially those that were on the outskirts that were in contact with Serb forces. That's where these groups were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yesterday you referred to Semso Salihovic as well as to a person called Becir Mekanic. And I quote you from transcript page 8, line 16: "As far as I know, there was quite a bit of disagreement among them. I think that they were in competition." What do you mean by that, "in competition"?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I wish to say by that is that someone was always trying to be the main authority in the area of Cerska. But of course no one ever succeeded in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What do you mean by main authority, a kind of chief commander?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the sense of a commander-in-chief but a person who would be trusted by most people from different groups. And people for the most part mostly trusted those who were the bravest. By your leave, Your Honours, I often said that when there was mutual assistance between Konjevic Polje and Cerska this was always done on a voluntary basis and people always went along with those who were the bravest. And those who were the bravest were certainly in greatest authority then, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Well -- what was then the reason of someone like those two persons mentioned of trying to become the authority or the top leader?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one tried to be the top leader. This really has nothing to do with government in power, but a leader in a different sense, someone who would be trusted. And if necessary, he could always have a bigger group of people trusting him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will now move to another issue. You also stated yesterday that groups were helping out each other, like Skugrici helping Konjevic Polje. Can you give an example of that assistance on both sides, as you call it.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Assistance always consisted of the following: For instance, when Konjevic Polje would be attacked, then at the invitation of people from Konjevic Polje, a certain number of volunteers would come from Cerska and help them out. The same happened when parts of Cerska were attacked. When we requested assistance from Konjevic Polje, a certain number of volunteers would invariably come to help us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And what's the reason for helping out each other? There were enough concerns for their own villages, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes. There was always concern for one's own village, but all villages were not attacked with the same intensity at any point in time. One village would be in the greatest peril and in that situation we would help out.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you. I will move to another issue, the issue of Nurif Rizvanovic. He came into the area in August 1992, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is it correct that Nurif Rizvanovic indeed had an idea of united forces?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What was the reason behind such a uniting of the forces?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The exact reason for his idea of uniting the forces is something I don't know. But yesterday I mentioned that I was in personal contact with him and that he thought that with the establishment of the so-called Drina Division, that is to say with the joining up of forces, he would manage to save the area from the enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will ask the usher now to show the witness D450. Your Honours, in -- it shows -- the translation shows 450 but I meant 415.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 415. What -- which document --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I just want to make sure that as far as the transcript is concerned that's rectified, but I want to make sure that the witness has 415 and not 450. All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: This document is bearing the head of a report -- reference is to it -- sorry. On the bottom there is a reference to "communication and information service of the armed forces of Bratunac and Vlasenica." My question is: Are you aware of any combined forces when it comes to communication and informations?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Isn't it true that by September 1992 a report like this could be sent to Sarajevo and Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: From where, Mr. Wubben?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: From Konjevic Polje. Thank you for this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Mr. Dedic, did you learn my question? Was it possible --

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, could you repeat the question in its entirety for me because I did not understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Repeat the question and I think we stop for a break because I'm noticing that the witness is getting gradually -- more tired.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Okay. I will stop -- I will stop --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just finish your question, repeat it again. But he has slowed down considerably and I think that's because he's feeling tired.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is it possible from -- is it possible to send a report like this from Konjevic Polje towards the Presidency in Sarajevo and the district staff in Tuzla, as far as you know, in September 1992?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my personal opinion, it was absolutely impossible to send this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I come to another --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we'll have a 30-minute break, starting from now. And, Mr. Dedic, Mr. Dedic, are you feeling tired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A bit, yes. I would welcome a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes. I will give you a 30-minute break. If after the 30-minute break you're still feeling tired, please tell us so much and we'll see what we can do. All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, Mr. Dedic, how are you feeling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That means we can continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If -- we have another -- just over half an hour left. We'll finish by quarter to 2.00. If in the meantime you think we ought to stop and send you back to the hotel, we will do so and then we will continue tomorrow. Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Mr. Dedic, yesterday you testified that in the beginning of November leaders of groups were invited to a meeting in Konjevic Polje elementary school and the issue was to link up the armoured group. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, actually I'm seeing "armoured" here and I'm wondering which armoured group you had in mind. And I don't know how it was translated to the witness anyway. I would imagine you mean "armed" group.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Armed group, indeed. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And in fact I was looking at you to see whether there was going to be some kind of reaction, but I immediately noticed that Mr. Di Fazio had caught the hint straight away. Yeah, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And I quote page 26 of the transcript from line 10 of yesterday: "Mr. Salihovic then gave some ideas to the effect that Mr. Oric could, according to Salihovic idea, be commander of all the forces from Cerska, Kamenica, Konjevic Polje, and Srebrenica." And further, line 19: "His idea was that all armed forces -" line 21 - "should be brought together, placed under a single command, because in his opinion that was the only way to resist the enemy because this was a time of very intensive attacks by the Serb forces in this area." Do you recall that testimony, Mr. Dedic?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: You added to it, and I quote: "To be quite honest, I thought that this was a very good idea and a very reasonable idea." Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that well. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Why was it such a good idea, a very good idea, and a very reasonable idea?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion it was a reasonable and good idea because Mr. Salihovic was very eloquent, and it seemed to me that what he was presenting to us was something that might save us from this agony. So he managed to convince me completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: You were convinced, so can you explain what was so very good about helping out regarding this agony when such an idea of unification would be implemented?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can explain because these groups up to that time had acted locally and only helped each other on a voluntary basis. What I expected to happen now was that they would truly unite, have a command, have units, and be able to function in a military sense and therefore be more successful. That was my conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Meaning also sharing information?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. Can you repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: United armed forces share -- enable those forces to share their information in a better way?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes. Yes. There would be a better exchange of information among the armed groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And was it correct that some villages had groups that were -- that consisted of a larger number of men than other villages?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The number of men in all the villages and all the groups was not the same. Some groups were smaller and some were larger.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And would such an idea of unification mean that the stronger will help out the weaker groups?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, in case of unification, stronger groups could of course help the weaker groups, so while the weaker groups couldn't really help the stronger groups. That's quite logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Would a unified command also be profitable in that situation?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A unified command would have been a good idea in any situation, had it been possible. It would have been a good idea, had it been possible to create one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. Such a unitary command, would that help to concentrate forces rather in areas where defence is most necessary?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such a command would certainly have succeeded in that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And that is why you thought it a very good idea and a very reasonable idea?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I quote --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: -- from the transcript page 27 on line 3: You attended two other meetings. And line 16: "A decision was made to set up a War Presidency of the subregion, and the president of this War Presidency would be Mr. Salihovic. And to establish a staff of the armed forces of the subregion that would be headed by Mr. Oric, as commander." Now, Mr. Oric had been chosen as commander, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, as you yourself stated, was supposed to have been appointed commander of the armed forces of the subregion, and Mr. Salihovic, as you said, was to have been the chief of the War Presidency of the subregion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Why was Mr. Naser Oric, as such, mentioned as the commander? Can you explain.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Probably, I think, because Mr. Salihovic was from Srebrenica, because Mr. Oric was from Potocari, he was from the Srebrenica municipality. And he knew him well. So probably he felt that he might be the man, if a subregion was established, that he could be the commander of the staff of the armed forces of the subregion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you have been shown a document, a decision of the War Presidency, dated the 4th of November, 1992. A -- showing a decision on joining the armed forces of the municipalities of Srebrenica, Bratunac, Vlasenica, and Zvornik into the joined armed forces of the subregion. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So a decision had been taken as such, and when it comes to the commandership of Naser Oric being or becoming to elect -- to be elected as a commander, what makes him so special to become a leader in such a top position?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why he would be so special. The first time I saw Mr. Oric was in mid-March 1993 in Konjevic Polje. This is the opinion of Mr. Salihovic. Why he held this opinion, I can't know for certain. But I assume he knew him better than he knew the other local leaders who he might have considered.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yesterday you testified that the reason was because Mr. Oric was brave like a lion and that -- and that that's one of the reasons why he was chosen. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He had fought like a like a lion, like a dragon. That's how he described it yesterday. Yes, Madam Vidovic, what's your ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that might have been one of the reasons, because I heard from people that there was a man called Naser Oric who fought in the way I described. That might have been a reason, but Mr. Salihovic might have also had other reasons for proposing this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: But wasn't it true that the meeting as such had adopted and the decision I referred to reflected that the participants on the meeting agreed upon the set up of War Presidency and appointment of Naser Oric as the top commander?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that meeting we agreed, and that was the decision put down on paper. There's no doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, in your opinion, this was a good idea and at least a good idea in November 1992. Was it also a good idea in October, October 1992?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what idea you're referring to. Can you clarify, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: The idea of uniting the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The idea of uniting the armed forces had always been a good idea. It was a good idea in June, July, August, throughout the time we were active in that territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dedic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will now ask the usher to show the witness D80 -- 818.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you have in front of you this order dated the 19th of November, 1992, signed -- not signed --

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: -- with the name of the commander of the Drina Corps, Zivanovic. I will ask you now after quotation a part of it, and that's the second sentence: "In order to prevent passage to the enemy from Srebrenica to Cerska and back," and further on in the order in the paragraph 2: "Cut off the Srebrenica-Cerska corridor." Do you read that -- did you read it?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Cut off the corridor? I can't find the text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Number 1. Just behind -- you see on that page after the -- there is one line with just one word, [B/C/S spoken], and then there is number 1. It's [B/C/S spoken]. Can you see it now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I see that. I see it well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Now, your question, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: My question is: What was the reason to prevent passage to the enemy from Srebrenica to Cerska, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this a question for me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By your leave, before I answer I have to say that I'm not even aware there was a corridor. If there was a corridor, then we would have been able to pass through it without hindrance. There were only certain very risky places where one could attempt to pass through. Yesterday, if you recall, I said that a lot of people attempting to pass through those places which were not a corridor were killed or wounded. So I'm not aware that there was a corridor that could be used to go to Srebrenica and back.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, do you agree with me that the Drina Corps command was apparently worried about this corridor being used by the enemy from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were worried or not, but according to what it says here, they wanted to solve their worries by preventing people from going anywhere from this enclave.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: At the time, November 1992, did indeed Muslim forces went from Srebrenica to Cerska?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I told you yesterday that only occasionally from time to time did some people manage to pass through and come back alive. No groups, whether armed or unarmed, could pass through, but only small numbers of people. And I repeat again, very often they were either killed or seriously wounded trying to pass that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you. That's for this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Madam Usher, will you please show the witness document D819.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I read this is a decision to attack dated the 3rd of December, 1992, shown to you yesterday. It's a document from the Bratunac Brigade command. Do you recall seeing that document yesterday?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, I will go to this part in paragraph 4 and paragraph 5, 6, 7, 8, and 9. In these paragraphs, and I quote: "In various ways the Bratunac command expressed their aim for the attack." Their aim for the attacks on those nine paragraphs is, and I quote in the middle of paragraph 4: "The aim of smashing Muslim forces." In paragraph 5, the third line: "Destroying the Muslim forces." In paragraph 6: "To destroy the Muslim forces." Paragraph 7 in the middle: "Also destroy the Muslim forces." Reiterated in paragraph 8 in the middle: "Destroy the Muslim forces." And paragraph 9, second line up to paragraph 10: "Tie down the Muslim forces." And three lines above that: "Inflict as many casualties on the Muslim forces as possible." Mr. Dedic, this refers to various areas within the area of responsibility of the Bratunac command. Why were -- why was the Bratunac command so worried about those Muslim forces? What frightened them? What made them attack -- what made them make such an order, a decision to attack?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, firstly I don't know really whether this witness can comment on what was going through the mind of Lieutenant Colonel Borivoje Tesic and the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He can tell us that himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: -- and moreover what frightened them. There's no indication here that they're frightened, maybe they're just smashing Muslim forces. He shouldn't put something in which isn't in the document really.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour, this is already guiding the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, but it's actually -- because it's not necessarily being frightened. When one decides to attack another, it's not because he or they are necessarily frightened. It could be strategic. Let's not discuss -- I would suggest that you use a very neutral expression: "Why would the Bratunac Brigade be so interested in causing all this destruction in amongst the Muslim forces?" and leave it at that. Because it may have been just strategic, it may well have been that they were afraid; I don't know. I mean, as Mr. Jones said, actually, I was not in their mind and the witness was not in their mind. He can only speculate. But if he does have a good reason or a good explanation for this, let him come forward and answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So, Mr. Dedic, the question is: Why would the Bratunac Brigade be so interesting in causing all this destruction among the Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday you probably noticed in Mr. Zivanovic's speech that winter was an ally of the Serbs. They knew well that in those areas we no longer had any food, clothing, footwear, that more than 70 per cent of the residential housing had been destroyed, and that this was a time when the Serb forces would be able to take control, full control, over this territory with the least problems. That's my interpretation. But why Mr. Zivanovic wrote what he did, that's something I cannot comment upon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I noticed earlier on that you wished to say something, Ms. Vidovic. Do you still want -- need to say what you meant to say?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because this might occur with the following documents, I will say this: Mr. Wubben is interpreting the document as if it happened in more than one area, but this document describes a very specific area; Bratunac-Kravica-Banjevici. This is precisely the Kravica area, it's not various areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that comment, Madam Vidovic. Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Mr. Dedic, in paragraph 11 of the document. Yes, paragraph 11 deals with the issue of command and communication. And I quote: "Use courier communications until attack commences. During attack, use radio communications." Are you aware of any reasons why only during the attack radio communication should be used?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, I haven't found that part. Let me have a look again. I have paragraph 11, where it says, "command and communications," but what you just read out now is something that I didn't manage to find in here, not yet at any rate -- oh, sorry. "Use courier communications until attack commences. During attack, use radio communications."

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, my question, rephrased, is: Why should there be a radio silence prior to the attack?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic could probably give you a better answer to that question, or one of his superior -- or rather, one of his officers who wrote this. I really cannot say anything by way of comment as to what his underlying idea was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Isn't the answer that - and I suggest it to you - that the Muslim forces had the ability to intercept the radio communications?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no comment regarding that statement of yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Madam Usher, that's enough for that document. Document D820, please, can you show that to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: D820, I apologise, has been shown to you yesterday. It was -- it is the decision by Colonel Milenko Zivanovic of the Drina Corps command. And I refer to paragraph 1 and will ask you for any comment. I quote: "The enemy -" on the second line - "in the general Srebrenica-Zepa-Cerska sectors and Kamenica area towards Zvornik, the enemy forces are rather strong and their number is increasing from 10.000 to 15.000 armed soldiers." Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely no. Had there been 10 to 15.000 soldiers there, I'm sure that Zivanovic would not have been where he was. That's not even close to what the actual situation on the ground was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And in the third paragraph -- sorry, not the paragraph, has no number. So we are still on this chapter 1, and then the third paragraph starting with the word: "Enemy forces of one reinforced company strength have been deployed in the Kravica river valley." "In -" further on - "In the Cerska area, the strength of enemy forces is increasing to 2.000 armed soldiers." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. During the course of the day I gave you an answer to this question. My estimate is that in Cerska there were about 2.000 able-bodied men. As for armed men, there were 400 to 500 of them. To my knowledge, these numbers are an exaggeration, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Let's move to page 5 of this order -- I mean page 5, the English version. That's paragraph 6, or chapter 6, on commanding and communication. Can you read that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Page 6 in Bosnian as well -- page number is at the top. At the bottom of that page is number 6 [B/C/S spoken]. Can you follow from there? Have you found it? Mr. Dedic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will quote the third sentence of that chapter: "Ensure complete secrecy in the commanding of units when preparing and conducting combat operations. "Use general KZ, cryptographic protections, documents (code cable, signal tables and coded maps, et cetera) for all written and spoken communication --"

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we are not receiving an interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we need to address that problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Prosecutor please repeat his question. Most of the Prosecutor's question was not interpreted. We've just started receiving the interpretation now. So could the Prosecutor please repeat his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly, Madam Vidovic. Mr. Wubben, please could you kindly repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will quote two sentences and then ask for your comment, Mr. Dedic. I will start the quotation now. "Ensure complete secrecy in the commanding of units when preparing and conducting combat operations. "Use general KZ cryptographic protections/documents (code tables, signal tables, encoded maps, et cetera) for all written and spoken communication of information." Again, my question is: When it comes to communication and preventing -- prevention of intercepts via radio communication, doesn't this document express the presumption that the Muslim forces were indeed able to intercept that communication?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I could not give an affirmative answer to your question. As far as I know, Muslim armed groups were not able to do what you mention in this document, to carry out any interceptions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you. I will move to another area and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We need to stop on time because I have an important appointment as soon as I finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Then it would be better to stop by now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So, Mr. Dedic, we'll give you another rest. You will go back to your hotel, and you will return back here tomorrow at 9.00. We are sitting in this same courtroom at 9.00 in the morning, and we'll hopefully try and finish with your testimony tomorrow. In the meantime, you are not to communicate with anybody on the subject matter of your testimony. All right. Anything else before we rise? Thank you, and we will continue tomorrow.
